ai_root_cause: Port security or MAC learning issue
corrected_diagnosis: Root cause was actually an incorrect VLAN assignment on the port, not port security — the port had no security config at all
notes: AI hedged between two possible causes without enough evidence to distinguish them, defaulting to the more common one (port security). Reviewer checked port config directly and found no port-security applied; the real issue was a VLAN misassignment. Good instinct to flag medium confidence, but AI should have suggested checking VLAN config as an alternative next_command.

ai_root_cause: STP blocking the only active link
corrected_diagnosis: Confirmed this was a genuine STP misconfiguration (accidental redundant link with default priorities), not just 'the only link' as initially assumed
notes: AI reasoned correctly that STP was blocking the port but appropriately flagged uncertainty about whether it was legitimate redundancy or a misconfig. Reviewer confirmed a second unused physical link existed, which explains the blocking, and adjusted STP priorities to resolve it.

ai_root_cause: NAT UDP timeout too aggressive
corrected_diagnosis: Timeout value was actually within normal range; the real issue was the VoIP application's keepalive interval was misconfigured to be too long for standard NAT behavior
notes: AI's diagnosis direction (NAT UDP timing issue) was reasonable given only TCP entries appeared in translations, but the fix target was reversed — the application's keepalive setting needed adjustment, not the router's NAT timeout. Still a useful starting point for the investigation.

ai_root_cause: Wireless channel interference/overlap
corrected_diagnosis: Actual cause was AP overload/insufficient AP density in a high-user-count area, not channel interference — channel utilization was high because too many clients were on one AP, not due to overlapping SSIDs
notes: AI's confidence was appropriately marked low, which was the right call, but the conclusion pointed away from the real issue. Reviewer performed a site survey and found only one AP covering a dense client area with no actual channel overlap from neighboring APs. This case is a good example of why AI diagnoses need human field verification before acting.
